metadata.unit_title: Working with speech and extracted information · Level 2
metadata.unit_slo: Distinguish speech AI from information extraction in common workplace tasks.

evaluation_context.goal: Produce an excellent, source-faithful learner session while preserving all deterministic correctness, identity, and sequence constraints.
evaluation_context.source_fidelity_goal: Independently verify the hard-gated edited challenger against the supplied source material. Reject unsupported facts, answers, explanations, feedback, or terminology changes; do not edit the artifact.

criteria.factual_fidelity: Every claim and answer is faithful to the supplied source.
criteria.answer_unambiguity: Each item has one defensible answer under its instructions.
criteria.distractor_plausibility: Distractors are credible without becoming defensible answers.
criteria.misconception_quality: Wrong choices diagnose realistic learner misconceptions.
criteria.cognitive_progression: The ordered session builds understanding at a coherent pace.
criteria.mechanic_rhythm_variation: Mechanics vary naturally without disruptive repetition.
criteria.scenario_authenticity: Scenarios resemble credible decisions or tasks.
criteria.feedback_usefulness: Feedback explains the governing concept and next step.
criteria.difficulty_appropriateness: Difficulty matches the stated audience and session position.
criteria.terminology_consistency: Terms are used consistently with the source and across items.
criteria.overall_learner_experience: The exact final sequence is coherent, varied, and instructive.

evidence.statement: Definitions and scenarios for speech-to-text, text-to-speech, OCR, information extraction, and speech capabilities generally match the supplied source.
The serial-number item identifies the source's information-extraction example, but its wording also overlaps with the source's OCR and computer-vision descriptions.

Most answer keys are mechanically determinate, but item 9 asks what finding serial numbers in an image is while rejecting both OCR and computer vision, which are also source-supported descriptions of that operation.
Distractors usually represent credible confusions such as text-to-speech versus speech-to-text, OCR versus speech recognition, and image classification versus information extraction.
The meeting-record item has three near-synonymous correct options and only one distractor, reducing contrast between alternatives.
Several distractors diagnose realistic direction, modality, and purpose confusions, including confusing vocalization with transcription, image text with audio, and image labels with extracted fields.
The serial-number item treats OCR as merely supporting the task even though the unqualified stem can elicit OCR as a reasonable mechanism-level misconception or answer.

The sequence begins with definitions and ordering tasks, moves into workplace applications at items 5 through 7, then returns to remembering-level fill-ins at items 8 and 9 before resuming application, creating a mild regression in cognitive demand.
The ordered session alternates multiple choice, multi-select, fill-in, and sentence-arrangement mechanics across the 13 items, with no long uninterrupted run of one mechanic.

Prompt stems vary across definitions, scenarios, fill-ins, and arrangements, but the multi-select wording repeats the same 'Which choices ... Select all that apply' pattern and arrangement prompts remain formulaic variants.
The receipt expense claim, meeting transcription, museum microphone interaction, article read-aloud, and technician serial-number tasks resemble credible workplace or public-service decisions.

Applying items commonly provide intrinsic and instructional feedback for incorrect options, but the first speech-to-text and information-extraction multi-choice items leave every option's feedback field null and rely mainly on generic rationales or item-level explanations.
The session mixes foundational recall with applying common workplace tasks, matching a Level 2 overview, although items 8 and 9 are low-demand repetitions after earlier application items.

Speech recognition, speech-to-text, speech synthesis, text-to-speech, OCR, and information extraction are mostly used consistently, but item 12 is keyed and labeled as speech translation even though its content describes general spoken interaction.

The sequence is generally coherent, varied, source-aligned, and scenario-based, but one item has a deterministic identity mismatch and another has unresolved answer-level ambiguity; feedback coverage is also uneven.

critical_defects.summary: The serial-number fill-in has multiple source-defensible interpretations.

evidence.statement: The stem 'Using AI to find serial numbers in an image is ___' is keyed only to information extraction, but the source also defines OCR as locating text in an image and computer vision as analyzing visual input; no wording limits the answer to the broader task category.

critical_defects.summary: Item 12's identity metadata says speech translation while its content tests speech capabilities.

evidence.statement: The item key and concept_id are 'speech-translation', but the prompt and answer describe accepting a spoken question and returning a spoken answer in the same interaction; the source defines speech translation as translation between languages.

largest_gap.summary: Feedback is not consistently learner-facing at the option level.

evidence.statement: Items 1 and 2 set every option's feedback field to null, so incorrect learners do not receive a direct misconception explanation and next step despite the availability of only generic rationales and item-level correctness explanations.

largest_gap.repair_instruction: Add concise per-distractor feedback that names the governing distinction and gives the next-step rule, while preserving the existing answer keys and sequence.

result.concise_summary: The session is mostly source-faithful, varied, and scenario-authentic, but item 9 fails answer unambiguity and item 12 violates concept identity. Confidence is reduced because no approved references were supplied.

history.stop_evidence: Critic requested human review or confidence was below threshold.
